text:
Anita: Heads-up — hit a weird async/runtime error when using the Python async SDK inside a FastAPI background task with uvicorn. Minimal repro below, stacktrace included. Anyone seen this?

Anita: ```py
# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")

async def poll_loop():
    while True:
        await client.generate("ping")
        await asyncio.sleep(1)

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup_event():
    # run in background (repro)
    asyncio.create_task(poll_loop())

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {"ok": True}

# run with: uvicorn main:app --reload
```

Anita: Error on reload sometimes:```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 247, in __enter__
    self._loop.run_until_complete(self.__aenter__())
```

Mike: Oof. Does the SDK call asyncio.run() internally when creating the async client? That would break inside uvicorn's loop.

Sarah: I saw something similar when the SDK had a sync wrapper that lazily called `anyio.run()` for background auth refresh. Are you using token refresh or sync convenience calls?

Anita: No explicit sync calls. Just AsyncClient(...). Repro is flaky — happens on reload/hot-restart. Stacktrace points to httpx client context manager being used from sync code path during import.

Tom: Quick guess: uvicorn's auto-reload spawns a subprocess and the import path might run sync init logic. Could be the SDK doing sync fallback if loop isn't ready.

Mike: Can you paste the SDK import path? any code that uses contextmanager like `with Client(...)`?

Anita: Only `client = AsyncClient(...)` at module scope. But the SDK's AsyncClient does some background task registration in __init__ that ends up calling `asyncio.run` under rare race.

Sarah: Repro suggestion: move client creation into startup event (so it's created inside the running loop) or create via `async def lifespan` to be safe.

Anita: Confirmed — moving to startup_event and `await client.aenter()` fixes the crash. But we shouldn't require users to remember that.

Tom: SDK feature request: support `AsyncClient.for_thread()` or a non-blocking init that defers loop-dependent work until first await. Also useful: explicit `from_thread()` helper to use async client from sync contexts (similar to httpx's `AsyncClient()` + `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`).

Mike: Another mitigation: lazy background tasks. In our code we use `self._bg_task = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_task(...)` during init. That will fail if called outside loop. Better to store coro and spawn lazily on first await or provide `start()` method.

Anita: I'll open a repro PR in the SDK. For now adding a short note to onboarding docs about not instantiating async client at module import time.

Sarah: Would be great if SDK raised a clearer error when created outside loop (e.g., RuntimeError: AsyncClient must be created inside an active event loop — or provide `sync_init=True`).

Tom: Also seen a different symptom: `httpx._exceptions.LocalProtocolError: Can't call send while awaiting` when using the same AsyncClient across threads (uvicorn workers). Need to document thread-safety and recommend per-worker client instantiation.

Anita: Added to the repro issue: flaky on reload, definite when module-level init + uvicorn reload.

ci-bot: Created issue redwood/redwood-python-sdk#432 - "AsyncClient: init outside running loop causes RuntimeError in uvicorn/fastapi reload". Link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk/issues/432

Mike: For immediate fix we can ship a minor patch: 1) avoid asyncio.run() in __init__, 2) if no running loop, set flag `deferred_init=True`, 3) start background tasks upon first `await` or when `await client.init()` called.

Sarah: Also add docs/snippet:```py
# safe pattern (FastAPI)
app = FastAPI()
client = None

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup_event():
    global client
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="...")
    await client.__aenter__()  # or await client.init()

@app.on_event("shutdown")
async def shutdown_event():
    await client.aclose()
```

Tom: +1 on clearer error plus a small helper `AsyncClient.init_on_loop()` or context manager `async with AsyncClient.open_in_loop():`

Anita: Thanks y'all — will link the PR to the issue and add a short blurb to the devex guide. If anyone wants to help review the patch ping me. :thumbsup:

Mike: Happy to review. Also let's add a test in CI that runs uvicorn + reload to catch regressions (maybe flaky but worth a try).

Sarah: Filed a follow-up doc ticket to update the onboarding quickstart to warn against module-scope async client creation.

Tom: FYI leaving a quick note in the SDK CHANGELOG draft.

Anita: Closing loop — temporary mitigation added to examples and doc. Will follow up when PR lands.
